plain_words: On the lossy test networks (P2, P3 and B1), every snapshot a test client files as "lost" now needs a reason. The reason has to come from a record the client does not write: either the server's own log says it sent that client nothing at that moment, or the simulated network's own log says it dropped at least one packet of that snapshot. Any other "lost" snapshot counts against the client, and the mark needs zero of them on every run. A second check runs the other way: a snapshot the network dropped a packet of can never be filed as received whole. That proves the network's record does not claim losses that never happened. "It arrived too late" is not on the list, because on the simulated network nothing can arrive that late (the slowest packet takes about a fifth of a second, and the client keeps about one second of snapshots). Two planted bugs prove the checks work: a client that files a received snapshot as lost fails the first check (48 of 48 clients), and a network record that invents a loss fails the second.

exact_texts.lab_record:
The new record is tick.s.snap_link_lost_count, in npt-lab's room log (process room). It is written on every room tick record, beside hs.server_hash, with one entry per client slot (the run's clients entries, 0 included). Each value is the number of snapshot datagrams the room sent that client at that tick that npt-l1's fate log records as Lost (the loss draw) or Burst. It exists on L1 only.
npt-l1 (crates/l1/src/lib.rs) gets one read-only addition:
  pub struct DatagramCounts { pub sent: u32, pub lost: u32, pub burst: u32 }
  impl FateLog { pub fn server_datagrams_since(&self, from: usize) -> DatagramCounts }
It counts the Datagram entries sent server to client (Dir::Down) at fate-log index from on, by outcome. The canonical form and its hash (PM-0001-3's identity, l1 :341-398) do not change, and it takes no draw.
When and where (crates/lab/src/scenario.rs, run, the per-slot loop at :967-1017), for each slot at each room tick:
- Just before server.send(slot, ...) (:989): let from = net.with_fate_log(|l| l.len()).
- After it: let c = net.with_fate_log(|l| l.server_datagrams_since(from)).
- Check 1: c.sent must equal the number of groups take_datagrams gave when the slot has a session, and 0 when it has none.
- Check 2: non-empty groups must have room.client(slot).server_hash() non-null.
- If either check fails, the run returns Err. Its logs then end without footers, which the judge reads INVALID.
- The slot's value is c.lost + c.burst.
The join is exact because Server::send (:557-584) sends only that slot's groups as datagrams. Pings and pongs come from the pump inside Server::io (pump.rs:387-404, :467). The events a send applies push only Ack and Stream entries (l1 :1419-1464, :1543-1584, :1624-1665).
The values go to Logs::room_tick (logs.rs:495) through one new parameter, link_lost: &[u32], which writes s["snap_link_lost_count"] with n entries, padding with 0. The module texts (logs.rs:1-8, scenario.rs:1-27) name the record.
Measured totals go on npt-lab's summary line after 'decided lost at the stop N': '; measured snapshot datagrams S, lost by the link L (in bursts B)'. These totals are not read by the judge.
The plant runs in bites builds only. PM-0001-17/link-lost-overstated becomes LAB_BITES' third id (scenario.rs:204, :234-245). On each slot, it writes 1 at the first measured tick where c.sent >= 1 and c.lost + c.burst = 0.
exact_texts.readme:
spikes/netcode-proof/marks/README.md §1, in the `decoded_hash` paragraph. One sentence goes in after '...that tick is lost (`null`, `tick.s.snap_incomplete` 1), never the sentinel.' (README.md:66-67), and the following lines are reflowed to 120 columns:
On L1's P2, P3 and B1 a tick filed lost must have a reason in the room's or the link's record, never the client's own: the room sent that client nothing then (`hs.server_hash` `null`), or npt-l1 lost a snapshot datagram of it (`tick.s.snap_link_lost_count`, the room log); a stale drop is no reason there, since L1 delivers every snapshot datagram well inside the ring (PM-0001-17's `snap_lost_unexplained_count`; `snap_whole_despite_link_loss_count` checks the record the other way).
README.md:6 holds: this contract change ships together with npt-judge and its fixtures.

explanations.rule: At that tick the room coded that client neither a snapshot nor a full state: its hs.server_hash for that slot is null (room.rs:204-208; reset each tick at :299-300, set only at :1128 for a full state and :1357 for a snapshot). This covers the full state not yet acknowledged (NC-L10; room.rs:1087-1089), whether after the join, after an overflow resync, or after a B1 burst's forced resync. It also covers budget short (:1173-1176, :1201-1204), an encoder refusal (:1119-1122, :1343-1346), and a kicked client (:1047-1049, :1057-1063).
explanations.source_of_truth: The room's (server's) record: hs.server_hash in the room log (process room), written by npt-lab from ClientSlot::server_hash (logs.rs:534-564). npt-lab also asserts at each send that non-empty groups come with a non-null server hash.

explanations.rule: The room sent that client snapshot datagrams at that tick, and npt-l1's fate log records at least one of them as lost by the loss draw or lost in a burst (l1/src/lib.rs:1097-1100). In the room log this reads tick.s.snap_link_lost_count >= 1 for that slot at that tick. A datagram that arrived, however late or reordered, never explains. The list is closed: every other tick filed lost is unexplained, and the check is 0 unexplained. That includes a stale drop (on L1 no snapshot datagram can arrive after one 32 ticks newer: about 180 ms worst delay on P3 against the ring's 1.067 s, and nothing newer is sent while a full state is in flight), a full-state tick filed lost, a tick whose datagrams all arrived, and a tick decided lost by the lab's stop (never inside the measured window of a valid run: scenario.rs:1126-1137).
explanations.source_of_truth: The link's record: npt-l1's fate-log entry of each snapshot datagram, which records the outcome decided at its send. npt-lab joins each entry to its (client, tick) at that send (the new record) and checks it one to one against the groups. The record is never taken from any client counter (stale, refused, duplicates).

conditions_met.id: ADV-C62H-2 (1): staleness from the link's record, never the client's counters
conditions_met.how: No explanation reads a client counter (stale, refused or duplicates; client lib.rs:381-401). The closed list has no staleness reason at all, because the link's own model rules lateness out on L1. A snapshot datagram's delay is at most one_way + half_jitter (l1 :215-221, :790-814), and the reorder step adds at most one more delay (:1134-1146): about 180 ms worst case on P3. The client's ring holds 32 ticks, 1.067 s (sim ticks.rs:58-70). While a full state is unacknowledged the room sends that client nothing newer (room.rs:1087-1089). So a stale drop on L1 is always unexplained, which is stricter than the condition and closes the read's hiding place (c). If the advisor wants lateness as a reason (C62HB-Q1 (b)), it is computed from the fate log's arrival order, never from the client.

conditions_met.id: ADV-C62H-2 (2): ticks the room sent no snapshot for are not unexplained
conditions_met.how: E1 reads the room's hs.server_hash null for that slot and tick (room.rs:204-208). That covers NC-L10's gap after a full state until it is acknowledged (room.rs:1087-1089), whether after the join, an overflow resync, or a B1 burst's forced resync. It also covers budget short, refusals and kicks. Ticks a B1 burst swallowed were sent and burst-lost, so E2 explains them. P3 s1's 27 overflow resyncs in the re-run set exercise this on a judged run.

conditions_met.id: ADV-C62H-2 (3): a new record of which client and tick each snapshot datagram carries; P2 and P3 re-run
conditions_met.how: npt-lab joins each snapshot datagram's fate to its (client, tick) at the send. The fate-log datagram entries pushed during one Server::send(slot) are exactly that slot's groups for that tick (pings and pongs come only from the pump in Server::io; scenario.rs:458-545, :557-584; pump.rs:387-404, :467). This is checked one to one, and the run fails otherwise. The lab writes their link-loss count per slot per tick as tick.s.snap_link_lost_count in the room log, using a new read-only npt-l1 accessor, FateLog::server_datagrams_since. The fate log's tick-less form and its sha256 stay as they are. The judged P2 and P3 sets are re-run, since old logs lack the series and would read INVALID, never PASS. B1 comes with U4g's judged runs.

- (b): a refused snapshot whose header tick reads far ahead moves the client's newest tick and files the whole span lost. On L1 those ticks were sent and delivered, so snap_lost_unexplained_count counts them. That is correct: it is the bug (b) fixes. questions.question: Should 'delivered too late' stay off the list of explanations?
questions.why: Option (a) as put to Mustafa (advisor-c62h-review-full.md:79) named it. Leaving it out changes the list he was shown (it gets stricter), so the wording to him must say so.
questions.options: (a) Leave it out. On L1 nothing can arrive after a snapshot 32 ticks newer (about 180 ms worst delay against the ring's 1.067 s; nothing newer is sent while a full state is in flight), so a stale drop is always a client error. (b) Build it from the fate log's arrival order: npt-l1 exposes arrivals, and npt-lab keeps each snapshot datagram's arrival per (client, tick) until written. That is about +70 lines that can never fire on L1, so the code can only ever hide an error if it is built wrong.
questions.recommendation: (a). The wording to Mustafa says plainly that 'too late' was dropped and why, and that this makes the bar stricter.

questions.question: Where should the comparison live: in the judge as two figures, or in the lab as two flag series?
questions.why: It sets the size, and it decides whether the program that writes the record is also the one that grades against it.
questions.options: (a) The judge: the lab writes only the facts (the room log's per-slot link-loss count), and two npt-judge figures compare them with the client's filing. Fixtures pin every case of the closed list, the same figures can serve L2 later, and this is how -17's coverage rule already works (figures.rs:316-536). About 520 lines, and JDG-ONLY-1 rides by its standing home. (b) The lab: npt-lab writes tick.s.snap_lost_unexplained and tick.s.snap_whole_despite_link_loss in the client log, and the checks are plain measured sums with no judge change. About 390 lines. The two bites still guard it (whole-as-lost would read Missed if the flag code were broken).
questions.recommendation: (a), with the exact texts given here.

risks: A mechanism I missed could make a correct client file a tick lost with neither E1 nor E2. The re-run sets would then show unexplained ticks, and the unit stops and tells Mustafa (history.md:2145). My read of every filing path (client lib.rs:492-615, :717-839) found only those two for npt-client on L1, and stale and sentinels are 0 on every judged run.

The join assumes Server::send sends only snapshot groups as datagrams. A later change that sends pings or other datagrams there breaks the one-to-one check, and the run fails loudly rather than writing a wrong record.

Disk: the P2 and P3 sets need 4,983.6 MiB and 4,620.4 MiB free at their starts (the runner's own check). The card had the build phase near 4.2 GiB, so KEPT-LOGS' pack (KL-YES, its own kit PR to main first) may have to come before the runs, delaying them.

A double fault can still hide: a lab record bug placed exactly where a client bug is. The two-sided checks, the two bites and the clean runs' 17k to 43k real losses make this narrow, but it is not zero.

The checks read the measured window only. Ticks the lab's stop decides lost (24 to 33 per P2 run, all in the after phase) are never checked. On a valid measured run, no stop decision can fall in the measured window (scenario.rs:1126-1137).

The summary line gains a phrase. c-u4r-runs.mjs reads 'overflow resyncs N' from that line, and the phrase goes after 'decided lost at the stop', so the runner's flag read must be confirmed on a dry plan before the sets.
The P2 set changes shape: it now has bites, so two judge calls and the split line, where U4r's P2 had one call. Its runs.txt is not line-for-line comparable with fc411116c1f1's.
Still unbounded after this lane: -58's two wrap parts (C62HB-Q4), -17's L2 parts (R3), and -17's L1 B1 part until U4g makes it valid. B1's (c) report line stays until then.

The bites build must run seed 1 the same as the measured build for the 'equal fate log' and '+48' expected lines. P0's whole-as-lost run (0 + 48) supports this, but on P2 it is unproven until the set runs. If it differs, the reason comes to the advisor.
The new checks are a stricter reading of ADR 0001's -17 row (row sha256 3075f638..., unchanged). Mustafa's yes to the wording is the decision, and the readings PR still lists them.
fallback_b: Not needed. Option (a) can be built cleanly. npt-l1 decides every snapshot datagram's fate, lost or not, at its send (l1/src/lib.rs:1097-1105), and npt-lab sends each slot's groups for one tick in one Server::send call, with nothing else sent as a datagram in that call. So the lab can join every fate to its (client, tick) exactly at that point, checked one to one, through a small read-only npt-l1 accessor and without keeping the fate log.
